messages:
noah r: Hey team, first week — hitting a weird local DB issue on my M1. Using Docker Desktop + compose v2. Postgres keeps failing on init when I mount ./pgdata. Error: 
```
initdb: could not create directory "/var/lib/postgresql/data/pgdata": Permission denied
```
noah r: I tried `chmod 777 ./pgdata` and restarting but it still fails. Anyone have reproducible fixes?

anya (eng): welcome Noah! :wave: This is typical on macOS bind mounts. Two reliable options: 1) switch to a named docker volume; 2) run a chown inside a container to fix ownership. We generally avoid host bind mounts for DB data.

jules infra: also check whether you're on Docker Desktop's new gRPC FUSE or using osxfs. gRPC FUSE can change semantics. If you use Colima (or Lima) the mounts behave differently and sometimes avoid the permission problem. If you prefer Docker Desktop, named volumes are the easiest fix.

noah r: hmm we use a compose file that mounts `./pgdata:/var/lib/postgresql/data` because some devs like files visible locally. If I switch to a named volume, how do I keep the existing DB?

anya (eng): copy the data into the named volume using a temporary container: 
```bash
# create named volume
docker volume create redwood_local_pgdata
# copy host folder into the volume
docker run --rm -v $(pwd)/pgdata:/from -v redwood_local_pgdata:/to alpine ash -c "cd /from && cp -a . /to"
```
Note: if host files are root-owned, the copy will preserve ownership; you can run a chown inside a postgres container afterwards: 
```bash
docker run --rm -v redwood_local_pgdata:/var/lib/postgresql/data --platform linux/arm64 postgres:15 sh -c "chown -R 999:999 /var/lib/postgresql/data"
```
999 is postgres uid in official images.

jules infra: also check image architecture. On Apple Silicon Docker sometimes runs amd64 images under qemu which behaves oddly. In compose add `platform: linux/arm64` for the postgres service to force native image. Example snippet we use: 
```yaml
services:
  postgres:
    image: postgres:15
    platform: linux/arm64
    volumes:
      - redwood_local_pgdata:/var/lib/postgresql/data
    environment:
      POSTGRES_USER: redwood
      POSTGRES_PASSWORD: localpass
      POSTGRES_DB: redwood_dev
      PGDATA: /var/lib/postgresql/data/pgdata
    ports:
      - "5432:5432"
volumes:
  redwood_local_pgdata: {}
```

noah r: I switched to a named volume and added platform, Postgres boots. But our `scripts/db-reset` still runs host `dropdb` and fails because host psql can't access the docker volume files. Any recommended pattern to update scripts?

anya (eng): we avoid host-level DB ops. Replace host `psql`/`dropdb` with in-container commands. Two patterns: 
- `docker compose exec postgres psql -U redwood -d redwood_dev -c "..."`
- or run a one-off psql container on the same network: 
```bash
docker run --rm --network $(docker compose ls -q) -e PGPASSWORD=localpass postgres:15 psql -h postgres -U redwood -d redwood_dev -c "SELECT 1"
```
Make scripts idempotent by using the compose project name and env file.

jules infra: small tip: if you really want host-native Postgres for speed, install via Homebrew and add `.env.local` to point DATABASE_URL at it. But we standardize on containerized DBs for parity with CI. Also Colima gives better mount behavior for some folks compared to Docker Desktop.

ops-bot: Dev setup reference: https://docs.redwood.ai/internal/dev-setup#postgres-local :link: 

noah r: Thanks — switching to named volume + platform and running CLI in-container fixed my workflow. I'll update my onboarding notes and open a tiny PR to add a Colima tip to the docs. Appreciate the help! :tada:
